facts.statement: Puntanipterus is an extinct pterodactyloid pterosaur found in the La Cruz Formation of San Luis, Argentina.
facts.quote: Puntanipterus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous period (Aptian stage) La Cruz Formation of San Luis, Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Puntanipterus was named in 1975 by José Bonaparte and Teresa Sánchez.
facts.quote: The genus was in 1975 named by José Bonaparte and Teresa Sánchez.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Puntanipterus globosus.
facts.quote: The type species is Puntanipterus globosus.

facts.statement: The genus name combines "Puntanos," the colloquial name for inhabitants of San Luis province, with the Greek word for wing.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to the Puntanos, the colloquial name for the inhabitants of the province of San Luis after the old name of their capital "San Luis de la Punta de los Venados", and combines this with a Latinized Greek pteron, "wing".

facts.statement: The species name means "spherical" in Latin, referring to the shape of the lower tibia.
facts.quote: The specific name means "spherical" in Latin, a reference to the form of the lower tibia.

facts.statement: The leg bones resemble those of Pterodaustro but feature an expanded spherical ankle joint and spiny processes on the tibia.
facts.quote: The leg bones were described as similar to those of Pterodaustro (from slightly younger rocks), except for having an expanded spherical joint at the ankle and spiny processes on the side faces of the tibia at that end.

facts.statement: In 1978, Bonaparte classified Puntanipterus as a member of the family Pterodaustridae.
facts.quote: Bonaparte in 1978 classified Puntanipterus as a member of the Pterodaustridae.

facts.statement: In 1980, Peter Galton concluded that Puntanipterus belonged to the family Dsungaripteridae.
facts.quote: In 1980 Peter Galton concluded it belonged to the Dsungaripteridae.

facts.statement: South American researchers argue that Puntanipterus and Pterodaustro are identical forms based on tibia comparisons.
facts.quote: This is by South American workers seen as a strong indication that both forms are identical.

facts.statement: Codorniú and Chiappe suggested in 2004 that Puntanipterus is a junior synonym of Pterodaustro.
facts.quote: Glut reported a personal communication from Laura Codorniú and Luis Chiappe (2004) that Puntanipterus should be regarded as a junior synonym of Pterodaustro

facts.statement: A 2009 study classified Puntanipterus as a valid dsungaripterid genus with morphology similar to Noripterus.
facts.quote: In a 2009 study, Puntanipterus was classified as a valid dsungaripterid genus and was considered to have a similar morphology to Noripterus based on comparison of known specimens.

facts.statement: Puntanipterus lived from the Late Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous and was found in the La Cruz Formation of San Luis, Argentina.
facts.quote: Puntanipterus es un género extinto de pterosaurio pterodactiloide posiblemente perteneciente a los dsungariptéridos que vivió entre el Jurásico Superior al Cretácico Inferior, siendo hallado en la formación La Cruz de San Luis, Argentina.

rejected.statement: The holotype, found in 1972, consists of a 105-millimetre tibiotarsus, a 7-centimetre fibula, a back vertebra, and wing and foot phalanges.
rejected.quote: It is based on holotype PVL 3869 (earlier FML 3869) found in 1972, a 105 millimetres long tibiotarsus and seven centimetres long fibula; referred to it were a back vertebra and a wing and foot phalanx.
